text:
alex: hi all! first-week environment weirdness. i installed brew on my M1-ish mac (Homebrew in /opt/homebrew) and asdf for runtimes. when i `asdf install python 3.11.4` it downloads ok but `python --version` still reports system python and `pipx` installs go to /usr/local. any idea why asdf shims arent taking? i tried restarting terminal and re-sourcing ~/.zshrc.

riya: welcome alex! common culprit is PATH order. asdf shims need to be before brew and system paths. can you paste the start of your `echo $PATH`? also post your `~/.zshrc` asdf lines.

alex: PATH snippet: 
```
/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin
```
and my .zshrc has the standard asdf line: `source $HOME/.asdf/asdf.sh` at the bottom after i added brew stuff.

gabe: looks like brew (/opt/homebrew/bin) is first, which is fine, but asdf shims live in `~/.asdf/shims` and must be inserted early. asdf installer usually asks you to add these lines *before* any other PATH modifications: 
```
. $HOME/.asdf/asdf.sh
. $HOME/.asdf/completions/asdf.bash
export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$PATH"
```
if you source asdf after overriding PATH or after direnv/other scripts, the shims can be appended instead of prepended.

alex: ah i see. i had `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` and my dotfiles append shims later. will move the asdf lines up. quick q: do i need to run `asdf reshim` after moving things?

riya: yes run `asdf reshim python 3.11.4` to regenerate shims. also check `which python` and `python -V`. if you use `pyenv` or a brew python, that can conflict. run `type -a python` to see all.

gabe: another note for mac users: some GUI apps (VS Code) launched from the Dock don't inherit your shell PATH. if you rely on the VS Code UI terminal to get the right PATH, either launch code from terminal (`code .`) or add path modifications in `~/.zprofile` (zsh login file) so GUI apps pick it up.

alex: good call. i always open code from spotlight. i'll add asdf to ~/.zprofile at the top and then `code .` workaround for now. did `asdf reshim` and `which python` now shows `~/.asdf/shims/python`. python -V shows 3.11.4 — yay. pipx still went into /usr/local though when i installed black via pipx.

riya: pipx location depends on which python/pipx you used. run `python -m pipx --version` or `which pipx`. you might have an old pipx installed by brew. `brew list pipx` or `pipx --version` will reveal. if brew-installed pipx is in /opt/homebrew/bin, uninstall it and then `python -m pip install --user pipx` so it uses the asdf python's user bin (usually ~/.local/bin).

alex: `which pipx` returned `/opt/homebrew/bin/pipx`. removed via `brew uninstall pipx` and reinstalled with `python -m pip install --user pipx`. added `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` after asdf lines. `pipx install black` now puts binary in ~/.local/bin and `which black` points there. thanks! :tada:

gabe: sweet. one more zsh tip: if you use direnv, make sure you have `eval "$(direnv hook zsh)"` after asdf lines; otherwise direnv's PATH manipulation can stomp shims. order matters: asdf + PATH shim prepend -> direnv hook -> other exports.

alex: oh right i have direnv too. reordered and added a short comment in my dotfiles: `# asdf shims must come before other path changes and direnv hook` so future new-hires know.

devx-bot: Welcome @alex! If you'd like, we can add your dotfile note to the team onboarding guide. Open a PR to https://redwood.internal/docs/dev-setup and tag @devx.
